lead: Diana, Princess of Wales was a British environmentalist, born on 1 July 1961 in Park House.
She died on 31 August 1997 in Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital at the age of 36.
She has 5 credited works on public record and has been recognised with Order of the Virtues and Royal Family Order of Elizabeth II.
The sections that follow break down Diana, Princess of Wales's biography into quick facts, early life, career history, personal life and a year-by-year timeline.

sections.heading: Diana, Princess of Wales — Early Life, Family and Education
paras: Diana, Princess of Wales was born on 1 July 1961 in Park House, and holds British nationality. She was given the name Diana Frances Spencer at birth and is publicly known as Diana, Princess of Wales.

Public records name her father, John Spencer, 8th Earl Spencer and her mother, Frances Shand Kydd. She is a sibling of Jane Fellowes, Baroness Fellowes, Lady Sarah McCorquodale, John Spencer and Charles Spencer, 9th Earl Spencer.
She studied at West Heath Girls' School, Institut Alpin Videmanette and Riddlesworth Hall School.
She is recorded as speaking English and British Sign Language.
